dedupe_keys.name: hcai california hospital seismic safety data building level structural and nonstructural ratings with hazus collapse probabilities county compliance deadline extensions and construction cost of healthcare projects

description: These open tables show how well each California hospital building would stand up to a strong earthquake, and how much hospital construction is under way. They are published by the Department of Health Care Access and Information, which enforces the state's hospital seismic safety law. The main file lists 4,694 buildings on 423 general acute care hospital campuses, each with its structural performance category from SPC 1 (significant collapse risk) to SPC 5, the probability of collapse estimated with HAZUS in 2007 and 2010, a nonstructural category for anchorage of equipment and systems, its status and the facility coordinates. Companion tables give county compliance with the 2020 and 2030 deadlines, the deadline extensions granted by statute, and biweekly totals of healthcare construction projects and their cost by county since September 2013. The data are free and available to download as CSV with data dictionaries or through the CKAN API. Caveats: no licence is named on the dataset pages, coordinates are for the facility, not each building, many ancillary structures carry no rating, and collapse probabilities come from 2007 and 2010 assessments. Simulation uses: scenario earthquake loss and bed-loss estimates for California hospitals, prioritising retrofit, and tracking how the hospital stock changes over time. Related records: the HCAI hospital utilization and financial data (data-hcai-hospital-utilization-and-financial) share the same facility identifiers.

schema_summary: Ratings file: County Code, Perm ID, Facility Name, City, Building Nbr, Building Name, Building Status, SPC Rating (1 to 5), 2007 and 2010 Hazus Score (probability of collapse, %), HCAI NPC Rating, AB 1882 Notice, Latitude, Longitude; extensions file adds the SPC and NPC extension columns by statute; county compliance file counts facilities, buildings and SPC 1, 2 and 3 to 5 buildings and facilities meeting the 2020 and 2030 requirements; construction file: County, Data Generation Date, project status, Total Costs, Number of Projects
